says: Defaults: "A new project runs Opus everywhere, with medium effort for threads and low effort for the conversation." On 2026-11-19 threads defaulted to high effort, and the page then added that high "draws on your plan fastest". The conversation is the coordinator. It decides what becomes a thread and tracks threads, while each thread opens and lands its own pull request. Coordinator and thread model and effort are set separately. The page gives no reason for the low-effort default.

"For most everyday coding and knowledge work, we recommend starting with Claude Opus 5.5." "Claude Fable 5.2 is our most capable model built for your hardest technical work." "Claude Fable 5.2 is our strongest lead agent." Sets Opus 5.5 as the everyday model and Fable 5.2 as the flagship.

Figures are in results.csv as suite AA-Briefcase. Elo on long agentic knowledge-work tasks (91 tasks across four multi-week projects), with a 95% interval of about 8 to 12 points either way. The Claude Fable, Opus and Sonnet entries are labelled ""Default Fallback"". At the 2026-11-24 read the board was refit with two new models and every score moved by under 4 points. It is one of the nine evaluations inside the AA Intelligence Index, which is in the base, so it is not an independent source.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Design Arena. Human-preference Elo with cost and generation time, read from the page's own leaderboard API, updated Nov 24, 2026; 366,291 votes, 100 rows. Scores rose about 15 points across the board since Nov 20, including rows with no new battles, so treat that as a rescale. Opus 5.5 appears twice: 1454 at high and 1337 with no effort named. Fable 5.2 appears once (1378), with no effort named. Comparisons behind the entries the table uses: Opus 5.5 high 2,846, GPT-6 Astra max 2,570, Fable 5.2 1,912, GPT-6.1 Sol max 2,245, GPT-6.2 Astra max 1,824, Gemini 4 Carbon 1,181. Gemini 4 Neon (1392 on 212) and GPT-6.2 Sol (1289 on 247) are now listed on Overall Agentic, unflagged but on few comparisons; on Overall HTML both are still preliminary (under 3,000). Most models appear at one or two efforts, so it shows no effort curve.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Arena WebDev, with cost per task. Human-preference ranking of finished web apps, 1,047,754 votes across 164 models, page dated Nov 23, 2026. Fable 5.2 xhigh 1822, Opus 5.5 max 1820, Gemini 4 Carbon high 1769, Neon xhigh 1765, GPT-6.2 Astra max 1761, GPT-6.2 Sol max 1755, Hydrogen xhigh 1701, Argon high 1682, Grok 4.7 xhigh 1639. The page now labels Neon and Hydrogen xHigh where the 2026-11-20 read recorded high, and Grok 4.7 is now scored. No per-model votes or intervals shown. Read in the Orca browser, since arena.ai refuses automated requests.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Arena Creative Writing, with cost per task. Human-preference ranking on the default board, which controls for style. Page dated Nov 22, 2026, with 1,508,322 votes across 425 models; no per-model votes or intervals shown. Fable 5.2 max 1525, Gemini 4 Argon high 1521, Opus 5.5 high 1518, Carbon high 1518, Neon xhigh 1504, Hydrogen xhigh 1492. GPT-6.2 Astra (max, 1471), GPT-6.2 Sol (max, 1436), and Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1421) now have scores; on 2026-11-19 the GPT-6.2 models were listed without one. Read in the Orca browser, since arena.ai refuses automated requests.

source: Anthropic, help center, Claude Fable models on your plan
says: On Max, Ultra, and premium seats: "You can use up to 50% of your weekly usage limits on Fable models at no extra cost." Fable draws on the same weekly limit as the other Claude models and uses it faster. After that, the page offers usage credits or switching to another Claude model. On Pro and standard seats Fable runs on usage credits only.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Lechmazur Writing, the six rows read. Stories scored by a panel of models, last updated 2026-11-17, 67 models. The six rows read are at high effort. Ranks: GPT-6.2 Astra 1, Fable 5.2 2, Opus 5.5 6, Gemini 4 Carbon 19, Gemini 4 Argon 27, Grok 4.7 32. The 95% intervals for Astra (4.223 to 4.379) and Fable 5.2 (3.498 to 3.636) do not overlap. Fable 5.2 first refused 58 of 400 prompts and was retried. Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol are not listed. Read from the raw README. Epoch rated the benchmark "Flawed" on 2026-08-10 for grading changes without versioning, mixed judge panels, and uneven story completion, and the rating stood on 2026-11-24: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/lech-mazur-writing/review

source: Hacker News, Gemini 4 Neon launch thread
says: About eight commenters say Gemini 4 writes more natural English than Claude or GPT models. Most name Argon, not Neon. These are personal impressions with no measurement, read second-hand through a research pass.

source: Artificial Analysis, Coding Agent Index v2.1
says: Figures are in results.csv as suite AA Coding Agent Index. Each model runs inside its maker's own coding tool (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI), and the score is the mean of FrontierCode-AA 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.1, and SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA. Opus 5.5 was tested at max only, and Gemini 4 Neon at xhigh only. Attempts finished by a fallback model: Opus 5.5 max 77 of 966, Fable 5.2 high 51 of 966 (45 to 63 across its other efforts), none for Codex or Antigravity. Gemini 4 Argon's cost per task doubled to $13.67 on 2026-11-24 with its score unchanged. Same operator as the AA Intelligence Index, so it stays outside the base.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Vals Terminal-Bench, the 11 rows read, and suite Vals Terminal-Bench by effort. Every model runs in mini-swe-agent with one bash tool; scores are avg@3 over 66 tasks, 70 models. The page was updated 2026-11-19 and states no effort in its table; the page's data records the effort each model ran at (Anthropic high or max, OpenAI max, Gemini high or xhigh, Grok xhigh). Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 tie at 65.15, Sonnet 5.5 is 64.14. The by-effort chart covers 10 models and still omits GPT-6.2 Sol and Gemini 4 Neon. Same operator as the Vals Index, so it stays outside the base.

source: VentureBeat, launch-week developer reports on GPT-6.2
says: Second-hand and from launch week: several named developers report GPT-6.2 Astra stopping early on long builds and say they would keep Opus 5.5 for agentic work. A separate report quotes the Codex lead saying the model changed in the three or four days before release, so early reports may describe an older build. Read through a research pass, not directly.

"Most workloads start with Claude Opus 5.5." Its comparison table lists Sonnet 5.5 for "everyday coding, agent, and enterprise workloads", so Anthropic's sources disagree, and the Claude Code default settles it. On the API, Opus 5.5 defaults to medium effort and Fable 5.2 to high. Read from the raw page.

Claude Code "defaults to Opus 5.5" on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, and the Anthropic API. "No Fable model is the account-type default on any plan or provider." In Claude Code, "Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 default to medium", so Fable runs at medium there although its API default is high. Read from the raw page.

"Choose GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding, writing, and work across several sources." "For demanding work across code, apps, or research, choose GPT-6.2 Astra." Sets Sol as the everyday model and Astra as the flagship. The guide says to "start with the effort your client selects", and new Work chats start on Sol at Light (Medium in Enterprise). Codex CLI 0.171.0 (2026-11-20) made Sol "the default catalog selection". Read from the raw page.

Hydrogen brings "speed and efficiency for everyday coding". Carbon is "Our strongest reasoning model, built for complex software engineering, multimodal knowledge work". On the API, Neon and Hydrogen default to high thinking and Carbon to medium. Read from the raw page.
"While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency." Read from the raw page.

Antigravity's recommended default for "Most day-to-day development" is Orchestrator, which plans with a top-tier model (Gemini 4 Neon by default; Carbon, Argon, or Claude Opus 5.5 can be chosen) and implements with Gemini 4 Hydrogen by default. Gemini 4 Neon is the default for new conversations, and Hydrogen is the default on Free, Plus, and Pro trial accounts. Every Gemini model now defaults to Medium thinking; on 2026-11-19 Neon and Hydrogen defaulted to High. Carbon is now included on paid Google AI Pro as well as Ultra and Enterprise, within the shared Gemini quota. Gemini 4 Argon leaves Antigravity on November 30, 2026. Sets Hydrogen as Google's everyday model, since it does the work. Read from the raw page.

"For everything else, including code, use Grok 4.7." xAI names no separate everyday or flagship model, so Grok 4.7 is both. Grok 4.7 is the default model in Grok Build, and its API default reasoning is high. Read from the raw page.

source: Practitioner reports on effort, last 30 days
says: Report. Gemini 4 Neon: one Hacker News user found Neon at high faster and cheaper than Opus 5.5 at medium with similar results on a long monorepo port. Theo Browne found xhigh beat high on a 3D build. No practitioner reported Neon at medium for real work. Ultra users saw Gemini 4 models at high think 3 to 4 times less from Nov 18 until a fix on Nov 19, so some launch-week reports may reflect that. GPT-6.2 Astra: Codex defaults it to low, where GPT-6 Astra defaulted to medium. A reviewer who ran five builds at xhigh saw early stops only in secondary features, and a UX Planet author found its UI weak at high and decent at xhigh. Several users say it stops early, mostly without naming an effort. GPT-6.2 Sol: one user reads Sol 6.2 at medium as matching 6.1 at high. Opus 5.5: Anthropic's own video recommends medium, and users who name a setting split between medium and high. Fable 5.2: users who name a setting run high or above, as lead or for hard work. No one reported Fable at medium. Hacker News read directly. Reddit, X, and most other posts read only through search snippets.

Figures are in results.csv. Agents build interfaces in a real repository, scored on use of the product's design-system components; 6 products, 20 tasks, 280 runs, one run per task, 95% intervals of about 7 to 10 points. Each model runs in its maker's own agent at medium thinking, except Gemini 4 Carbon at high because Gemini CLI has no medium for it. Leaderboard dated Nov 12, 2026; methodology page Nov 16, 2026. Costs for Carbon and several open models are estimated from tokens. The operator is not named beyond "21st" and may sell UI tooling. GPT-6.2 models and Gemini 4 Neon are not listed. Read from the page's embedded data.

Professional writers judge creative, business, and everyday writing in blind pairs. The leaderboard read on this date lists 48 models and none of the current releases; its newest entries are Fable 5.1, Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol. Surge says Arena's quick votes "reward flashy formatting over substance." Surge sells evaluation work.

source: Stephen Smith, hands-on test of board and investor documents
says: Report. Ranks Fable 5.2 first ("the level of polish I would expect from a very seasoned consultant"), Gemini 4 Neon a close second, and GPT-6.2 Astra last ("wasn't in good enough shape"). Did not test Opus 5.5, GPT-6.2 Sol, or the other Gemini 4 models. Read through a research pass.

source: Practitioner reports on writing, last 30 days
says: Report. Many Hacker News users and Theo Browne praise Gemini 4 Neon's writing, mostly unprompted. They say it writes docs, landing pages, and comments better than Claude out of the box. One user says Neon with Diátaxis produced docs "indistinguishable from human writing". Theo says Neon wrote a plan as a blog post where Fable "cannot write in a way that feels like an actual blog". Argon still draws praise as Google's best writer, and one user calls Neon "as good as Argon" but faster. No one compared the two side by side. In Peter Yang's blind 300-word essay test, Gemini 4 Carbon beat Fable 5.2, and GPT-6.2 Astra won no round. Several users call Astra's prose hard to read. No post named a non-fiction writing benchmark that covers current models. Hacker News read directly. The rest read through a summarising reader or snippets.

source: Contra Labs x BenchFlow, Frontier Design Benchmark
says: Figures are in results.csv as suite Frontier Design. Blind head-to-head votes by professional Contra designers on websites built from 33 real client briefs, turned into Elo; 4,821 votes from 40 designers, data updated Nov 22, 2026. Human designers' own builds are ranked with the models (1735). No effort is named for any model; models ran through OpenRouter, in their own lab's harness where possible. Fable 5.2 1710 on 788 votes and Opus 5.5 1684 on 539 sit just under the humans; GPT-6.2 Astra 1755 and GPT-6.2 Sol 1631 are on only 114 and 111 votes. All four Gemini models sit 200 or more points lower: Neon 1430 (111 votes), Carbon 1337 (660), Hydrogen 1298 (114), Argon 1212 (553); Grok 4.7 1236. A stealth model, Gestalt, leads at 1932; Contra calls Fable 5.2 the highest-rated model it ran and says it works with Gestalt's team. Contra runs the freelance marketplace the briefs and voters come from, and the dataset is not public, so the board cannot be checked independently.

source: Practitioner reports on executors, last 30 days
says: Report. Gemini 4 Neon at high matched Opus 5.5 at medium on one user's long monorepo port at less than half the day's spend. Owain Lewis found Neon's implementation step cost $1 against Opus's $6, with no effort named. On short tasks Flavio Copes found Opus 5.5 faster and cheaper than Neon at every effort, and the only Neon-at-medium run was in that small test. One Hacker News user, writing mostly from Carbon, found Gemini models lose track on multi-day tasks where Opus does not. GPT-6.2 Sol: one r/codex user calls it "really good". A five-app review on Codex's top setting found clean builds with a rough finish. Two Hacker News users report over-engineering or skipped steps from 6.2 Sol. No report tested Opus 5.5 at high beside Neon or Sol at medium. Hacker News read directly. Reddit and reviews read through snippets or a summarising reader.

source: Practitioner reports on design, last 30 days
says: Report. Peter Yang gave Fable 5.2, GPT-6.2 Astra, and Gemini 4 Carbon the same briefs. He picked Fable overall and rated Fable and Astra comparable on a homepage redesign: Fable for motion, Astra for clarity. Carbon's pages and scenes felt dense or cluttered to him. A UX Planet author found Astra's UI weak at high and decent at xhigh. No one compared Gemini 4 Neon with Carbon on UI. Theo Browne found Neon weak at 3D visuals, and one Hacker News user found it better than Fable at iterating art assets. Peter Yang's tests read second-hand through a write-up. UX Planet read only through search snippets.

source: Practitioner reports on leads, last 30 days
says: Report. Theo Browne found Gemini 4 Neon more coherent than any Anthropic model on long work. He also found it gave real feedback on a plan that GPT-6.2 Astra had accepted as written. One Hacker News user's private long-horizon benchmark put Neon "far below Carbon" in quality, at a quarter of the time. Several users run Fable 5.2 as lead at high or xhigh over Opus 5.5 workers, and none at medium. Flavio Copes found that setup cut Fable's own spend by 61% but nearly tripled run time. Launch-week testers report GPT-6.2 Astra stopping early or stalling on long, self-directed work. Hacker News read directly. Videos and articles read through a transcript, a summarising reader, or snippets.
